uncited: *   **Input:** Volume dataset, transfer function (color $C$, opacity $A$), light color $C_L$, observer view direction, light view direction, frame buffer resolution.
**Eye Buffer:** Standard frame buffer storing the final composited color.
**Light Buffer:** An off-screen render buffer (pixel buffer) or texture.
It stores the accumulated light intensity arriving at each slice.
*   Calculate the dot product of the light direction ($L$) and view direction ($V$).
*   If $L \cdot V > 0$ (acute angle): Set the slice axis to the vector halfway between $L$ and $V$.
*   If $L \cdot V \le 0$ (obtuse or perpendicular): Set the slice axis to the vector halfway between $L$ and $-V$ (inverted view).
*   Render the current slice geometry into the eye buffer.
*   Render the same slice geometry into the light buffer.
Blend into the light buffer using the **Over** operator.
A technique that slices along major volume axes.
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of slices and the resolution of the buffers.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(W \times H)$ for the light buffer, where $W, H$ are the buffer dimensions.
